payload.pattern: A phantom human blocker inside a CURE freezes the fix permanently — and every studio phantom-blocker detector points at the task plane, not the doc plane.
payload.context: Obelisk remote CI was budget-blocked (not broken) for weeks. The free, studio-canonical fix (self-hosted runner, CANON-038) was written W217 in docs/CI_SELF_HOST_RUNNER.md and never ran, because the doc claimed the runner registration token needs a GitHub admin token — the only non-agent part. That is FALSE: it mints with the repo scope the studio gh auth already holds. Six consecutive sessions (W217-W222) read the cure, deferred CORRECTLY under CANON-019, and closed out founder may restore CI billing.
payload.insight: A phantom blocker in a TASK costs one item. A phantom blocker in a CURE is self-preserving: every diligent agent defers correctly, so diligence itself keeps the fix frozen. No amount of care dislodges it — only a machine that checks the claim.
payload.coverageGap: All three studio phantom-blocker detectors read ONLY context/TASK_BOARD.md: vaultspark-studio-ops/scripts/blocker-preflight.mjs:25, vaultspark-studio-ops/scripts/check-phantom-blockers.mjs:76, and obelisk scripts/blocker-preflight.mjs:26. The documentation plane, where cures are written, has zero coverage in every repo.
payload.solution: scripts/check-phantom-human-blockers.mjs + scripts/lib/doc-deferral.mjs (Obelisk W222, portable). Fires ONLY on positive evidence: a human-only assertion naming either a capability the secrets gateway reports READY, or a gh scope the studio actually holds. A naive marker scan hits ~380 times across docs/+context/, so precision comes from requiring evidence, never from tuning a threshold. Claims naming nothing checkable are unclassified and never fail the gate — unverifiable is not false.
payload.doctrine: A deferral is either a CAPABILITY gap or a JUDGMENT call and a written cure must say which. Declared judgment is annotated, not prosed: <!-- human-blocked: judgment|billing|hardware-key|provider-signup|destructive --> (the five CANON-019 reserved categories). Recording a judgment call as a capability gap manufactures phantoms; recording a capability gap as judgment hides real work.
payload.lesson: Operating the new detector against its own pre-fix corpus revealed it did NOT fire on its motivating case — that block names a GitHub credential, not a dotted capability. Root-fixed with a second evidence source (gh scope resolution), never a loosened threshold. Ship no detector without running it against the corpus that motivated it.

payload.pattern: deno test inherits NODE_OPTIONS and fails closed under the S195 Windows window-storm guard
payload.context: Any repo that both (a) uses Deno (edge functions, scripts) and (b) has the mandatory Windows window-storm guard installed (NODE_OPTIONS=--require windows-hide-shim.cjs) will see deno test/deno check fail with NotCapable: Requires read access, because Deno honors inherited NODE_OPTIONS but deno test grants no fs-read permission by default. This silently broke canon own test:edge-functions script for an unknown number of prior sessions.
payload.solution: Strip NODE_OPTIONS from the child env before spawning the Deno subprocess. See canon scripts/run-deno-edge-tests.mjs (S234) for a minimal safe-spawn-based wrapper. Do not disable the Windows guard itself, it is correct and necessary for Node children.

payload.pattern: lib/ark.mjs findStudioOpsRoot() sibling-fallback path math is off by one directory level
payload.context: Any sibling repo that copies scripts/lib/ark.mjs fresh (per the Lib Sync Pattern) and calls findStudioOpsRoot() with no arg gets __dirname == <repo>/scripts/lib. The sibling fallback paths (../../vaultspark-studio-ops and ../vaultspark-studio-ops resolved FROM scripts/lib) both land one level short of the true sibling of the repo root, so ship/drain/status silently fail with studio-ops root not found on every fresh sibling install. Only studio-ops own copy of this file works, because its primary walk-up loop finds its own manifest before ever reaching the buggy fallback.
payload.solution: Add a third fallback: path.resolve(startFrom, ..", "..", "..", "vaultspark-studio-ops") checked BEFORE the existing two, to correctly walk from <repo>/scripts/lib up past <repo>/ to its true sibling directory. Canon local-patched this in scripts/lib/ark.mjs (S234) as a stopgap per CANON-018; the canonical fix belongs in vaultspark-studio-ops itself.

payload.pattern: A scan that silently skips what it cannot parse narrows its own denominator and reports a clean result over the shrunken remainder — absence of a finding presented as proof of absence.
payload.solution: Make every scan emit {checked, skipped:[...with reasons]} and surface the skip count; a completeness/PASS claim over considered===0 (or an unmeasured remainder) fails. On weak-signal planes (e.g. options-object keys where the outer ={} default makes never-supplied normal) run ADVISORY not hard-fail, exclude seam shapes by construction, and baseline the semantic remainder — an over-detector is itself a vuln. For liveness gauges, classify the population by measurability (scheduled=history-measurable; event/tag/reusable/manual=UNMEASURABLE-FROM-HISTORY) instead of reading silence as green or dead.

payload.pattern: REVOKE EXECUTE FROM authenticated is insufficient for a SECURITY DEFINER function unless PUBLIC is also revoked -- Postgres grants EXECUTE to PUBLIC by default and every role inherits it. Any studio project using Supabase SECURITY DEFINER functions should audit for this.

Postgres SECURITY DEFINER functions remain callable via the implicit PUBLIC role even after REVOKE EXECUTE FROM authenticated/anon -- PUBLIC grants EXECUTE by default on every new function and every role inherits it.
payload.solution: Always REVOKE EXECUTE ... FROM PUBLIC explicitly (not just FROM authenticated/anon) when a SECURITY DEFINER function should be caller-scoped or service-role-only. Verify live with: SELECT has_function_privilege(role, function_signature, (quote)EXECUTE(quote)). A GRANT ... TO service_role list in a migration file does NOT mean other roles cant call it -- confirmed live this session where an explicit service_role-only GRANT was still exploitable via the PUBLIC default.
